rationale: Grouping is explicitly a presentation heuristic; users see original names, formats, and exact installation paths before any file action.
Keep is the default, whole-product selection is explicit, and removal is confined to selected validated bundles through macOS Trash without permanent-delete or privilege escalation fallback.
Scanned identity and symlink checks, overlap rejection, partial failures, and scan/removal exclusion define concrete safety and recovery boundaries.
Successful items alone leave the inventory; failed entries and associated evidence remain available.
Multi-root work extends existing persisted arrays without promising unlimited underlying filesystem capacity, and tests cover repeated additions and reopening.
Runtime Trash tests are limited to generated fixtures; implementation authority does not authorize deletion of the user's real audio content during development.
limitations: Specification critique only; implementation review must verify fail-closed handling when scanned identity is absent and truthful per-item Trash outcomes.
Grouping cannot establish product ownership or shared-content dependencies; confirmation and UI copy must retain that distinction.
Path-based Trash retains the disclosed final-validation race; no adversarial atomicity claim is approved.
No product code changed and no private content or .qa-criteria accessed.
